title: CAPIT FAQs | Data, Token, and Wallet Answers
description: Answers to common questions about CAPIT’s data, token mechanics, wallet flow, privacy, and strict claim boundaries.
headline: Frequently Asked Questions
body: Find clear, factual answers about CAPIT’s data ingestion, methodology, token flow, wallet interactions, and policy boundaries.

sections.heading: What is CAPIT?
sections.body: CAPIT is a public-facing environmental registry and utility token project built on the Base network. It organizes U.S. well-plugging records, explains their provenance, and shows CAPIT-linked protocol activity directly next to the underlying data.

sections.heading: How does CAPIT define a plugged well?
sections.body: CAPIT strictly follows the source-agency definition for the physical record being shown. When CAPIT normalizes terms into a sitewide display taxonomy, we ensure both the original source status and the CAPIT display status remain visible.

sections.heading: Where does the data come from?
sections.body: We rely on public, state-level well registry data. CAPIT identifies the source agency, source system, fetch date, verification date, and any caveats for every visible record set on the platform.

sections.heading: Why can the numbers change?
sections.body: Public records can be revised, corrected, reclassified, or expanded by state agencies. CAPIT preserves a visible, immutable revision trail instead of pretending the data is static.

sections.heading: Does each CAPIT token equal one well?
sections.body: Yes. CAPIT enforces a strict 1:1 ratio. Exactly one CAPIT token is minted for every unique, verified plugged-well record. This rule creates a permanent, non-inflationary record of environmental progress.

sections.heading: Does buying CAPIT fund plugging work?
sections.body: No. CAPIT is a transparency and tracking ledger. It does not directly fund physical remediation efforts unless a specific, publicly documented grant or revenue-allocation mechanism is officially described.

sections.heading: Is CAPIT a carbon credit or offset?
sections.body: No. CAPIT serves solely as a strict, source-linked environmental infrastructure receipt representing physical remediation. It is not a carbon credit, emissions offset, or speculative financial asset.

sections.heading: Do I need a wallet to use the dashboard?
sections.body: No. The data experience remains completely open and free to users who only want to read, search, and compare public environmental records.

sections.heading: What happens when I connect a wallet?
sections.body: CAPIT may receive your public wallet address, network, and connection status. CAPIT will never ask for your secret recovery phrase, private keys, or wallet password.

sections.heading: What network does CAPIT use?
sections.body: CAPIT is built securely on the Base network. The Buy page clearly shows the network and contract details before users proceed with any interaction.

sections.heading: Can CAPIT reverse a failed or rejected transaction?
sections.body: No. CAPIT cannot reverse blockchain transactions. Users should carefully review network, contract, approvals, gas fees, and wallet prompts before confirming any transaction.

sections.heading: Where can I review the contract details?
sections.body: The Buy CAPIT page exposes the token contract address, Base block explorer link, source repository link, and the latest approved token disclosure text.
